careful, don't get pricked
there's thistles, thorns and daggers
in the dark I climb the scaffolding
I see the city from up high
sleepless cat eyes
drop by drop fills the glasses

questions.issue: 'gota a gota colma vasos' = 'drop by drop fills the glasses' (idiom: little by little things overflow); kept literal in all versions.
'velita' + 'tirar la cera' reads as a candle/wax ritual or curse (witchcraft theme of the song), not literally pouring wax in a sexual sense; I kept it ambiguous.
'disociando entre gritos pelea y fandangos' - unclear whether 'pelea y fandangos' = 'fight and party' (fandango = ruckus/fiesta); translated as brawl and fandangos.

questions.original: y a partir de ahora mia
questions.issue: 'mia' (written without accent) could be 'mía' (your will is mine) or 'mi a(...)'; translated as 'mine'. Also 'no te quedes mal' could mean 'don't be left upset' or 'don't leave things half-way'.
'mago un moño' = 'hago un moño' (phonetic spelling); 'moño' could be a hair bun or an idiom (making a fuss); chose hair bun.
'nirea pairamena' (my suffering) is syntactically odd/dialectal; also unclear whether 'mozorrotuko dut' disguises the suffering or the speaker ('I will dress up').
'amarre' = mooring/tie but also a love-binding spell (amarre de amor); both meanings plausible. Also the subject of 'secuestró' (she/he/I) is unclear - rendered 'she'.

questions.original: te escucharé cuando el cora lo pueda resistir
questions.issue: 'cora' is a clipped 'corazón' (heart); also the shift from 'tiene' (3rd person) to 'te escucharé' (2nd person) is kept as in the original.
